finding_key: docs/design/documents-last-modified.md::new standalone top-level design doc for what is a single-pr backend fix, instead of folding into the canonical subsystem doc (backend.md / frontend.md)
evidence: The convention the claim cites exists verbatim: docs/design/README.md's "Obsolete docs" section says the durable design "lives in its canonical subsystem doc ... regardless of whether it shipped as a single PR" and to "Fold a single-PR note into the relevant doc ... rather than keeping it as a standalone file", and CONTRIBUTING.md says to "Update the existing doc when evolving an area instead of creating parallel files." The PR adds a standalone docs/design/documents-last-modified.md plus a README row while leaving docs/design/backend.md untouched — its ERD still shows Document with only createdAt and its env table lacks YORKIE_SECRET_KEY, so the canonical doc is now stale on exactly this change. The claim's own counter-evidence is fair, though: the Common section already hosts narrow single-feature docs (context-menu.md, comments-mentions.md, pdf.md), so this is a mixed-precedent organizational judgement, not a correctness or user-facing defect — hence nit severity and medium confidence.
